newsitem.title: DENMARK: Domestic, German data fail to move Danish bonds.
newsitem.headline: Domestic, German data fail to move Danish bonds.

text.p: Danish bond prices were unchanged on Monday, after domestic CPI and German M3 data came in as forecast, and Copenhagen dealers saw little prospect of change on Tuesday.
"Prices will stay at present levels and the yield spread won't move either," a dealer said, adding that no fresh indicators likely to awaken the market were due.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 finished at Fridays's closing price of 107.98, having traded up to 108.09 and back again during the day, in thin turnover of one billion crowns.
The benchmark's December future rose 0.29 point to 107.44, with 28 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.20 point to 85.30.
The crown currency ended the day at 3.8289, slightly down from earlier levels and only just up on Friday's closing 3.8290.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany remained unchanged at 83 basis points. --Kenneth Lund, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969651
